(a) school psychologists were generally unbiased; (b) traditional respondents evaluated the black pupil as more retarded than his white counterpart; (c) respondents with more traditional values recommended the black pupil for custodial placement more often than did other school psychologists.
school psychologists, like most other people, are influenced in their diagnostic and therapeutic recommendations by their own values and beliefs.
School psychologists are not biased against black children, and that they are not biased against children from lower socioeconomic backgrounds.

the effects of social class and race on psychoeducational decisions and on school psychologist expectancy-biases.
the social and political implications of the psychologist's diagnostic and therapeutic decisions.
the effects of the social class and race of the pupil on the psychoeducational decisions of the school psychologist.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data suggest the existence of a bias, but the bias is not strong and is not clearly defined.
school psychologists are not biased against the socially disenfanchised pupil, but that they are not immune to the influence of their environment.
, while school psychologists are not generally biased against the socially disenfanchised pupil, there are certain situations in which they may be.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the school psychologist, like the teacher, has a social bias that is more subtle than previously thought.
school psychologists, as a group, are less traditional in their thinking than are other psychologists.
school psychologist expectancy-biases against the socially disen-franchised child are not likely to be a major factor in psychoeducational decision-making, but that the issue is not yet closed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social class and race of the pupil can affect the school psychologist's psychoeducational decision-making.
the social class and race of a child can affect the way that school psychologist evaluate that child.
